column3: The Hebrew has both “spoke” and “saying”; BSB condenses these to “said.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew uses the fear verb for parents; BSB says “respect.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew repeats the sacrifice verb; BSB varies it with “offer.”
The Hebrew joins the sacrifice day and the next day with “and”; BSB uses “or.” The Hebrew also explicitly says the remainder is burned “with fire.”
The Hebrew emphasizes eating with a repeated passive verb; BSB says “any of it is eaten.”
The Hebrew ends with plural “her peoples” for the person being cut off; BSB uses singular “his people.”
The Hebrew uses singular “the edge of your field”; BSB uses plural “the very edges.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew gives three commands joined by “and”; BSB separates the stealing command, then joins lying and deceiving with “or.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says the hired worker’s wages must not “remain overnight with you”; BSB expresses this as not withholding them until morning.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew uses “lift the face” and “honor the face” for partiality and names a “great” person; BSB uses “show partiality,” “favoritism,” and “the rich.”
The Hebrew says not to “stand over the blood” of one’s neighbor; BSB interprets the expression as not endangering the neighbor’s life.
The Hebrew repeats the rebuking verb emphatically and says not to “bear sin”; BSB says “Directly rebuke” and “incur guilt.”
The Hebrew names “the sons of your people”; BSB says “any of your people.”
The Hebrew repeats “two kinds” for livestock, field, and garment, and says the garment must not “go up on you”; BSB uses “crossbreed” for livestock and “wear” for clothing.
The Hebrew retains the seed image in its description of intercourse; BSB says “lies carnally.”
The Hebrew names “his guilt offering” and repeats “a ram of a guilt offering”; BSB combines the expressions into a ram brought “as his guilt offering.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew describes the fruit with repeated circumcision language, including “foreskin” and “uncircumcised”; BSB renders it as “forbidden.”
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says not to eat “with the blood”; BSB adds “anything” and “still in it.”
The Hebrew says to “round” the head’s edge, without explicitly naming hair; BSB says to “cut off the hair” at its sides.
The Hebrew names an “inscription of an incision”; BSB says “tattoo marks.”
The Hebrew repeats “the land” as subject of the prostitution and filling clauses; BSB gives the subject once.
Close to the Hebrew.
